architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.text: Architecture MUSA uses Kotlin Multiplatform with Compose Multiplatform for the UI and SQLDelight for storage. Almost all the code lives in the shared module. The androidApp , desktopApp and iosApp projects are thin entry points. Layers The shared code under org.softwareanvil.musa is split in three layers: Layer Holds domain/ Models, repository interfaces, use cases and pure logic such as validation and filtering. data/ SQLDelight queries, mappers between rows and models, and repository implementations. ui/ Compose screens and their ViewModels, which expose state as StateFlow . Dependencies point inwards: ui and data depend on domain , and domain depends on nothing. Wiring Koin connects the layers in di/ . Each platform only provides two things: its SQLite driver and the folder where the database lives. Clocks and id generators are injected, so the domain logic can be tested with fixed values. Ids Every product, variant and tag has a UUID generated on the device. This keeps the door open to syncing with a backend later without renumbering anything.

events.title: Events
events.text: Events The events module tracks a fair or market: what stock goes there, what sells, and what the day really earned once costs and expenses are paid. An event An event has a name, a place, a start date and an end date. It is open while it can take stock and sales, and closed once it is over. Taking stock Stock moves from the catalogue to the event. Taking 5 prints lowers the catalogue by 5 and puts them on the event's list. You cannot take more than the catalogue has. While the event is open, the − and + buttons on a line move one unit back to the catalogue or bring one more. You can only give back units that were not sold. Only physical products can be taken to an event. Selling Each line has a Sell button. The sale starts at one unit and at the variant's price; both can be changed, for discounts or bundles. A sale stores the product and variant names, the price and the cost at that moment, so editing the product later does not change past totals. Selling lowers what remains at the event; the catalogue does not change, because those units already left it. A sale can be undone while the event is open. Its units then count as remaining again. Expenses Expenses are what attending cost: stand, travel, lodging, food. Each has a concept and an amount. Summary Figure How it is computed Units sold Sum of the quantities of every sale Gross Sum of quantity × price Cost of goods Sum of quantity × cost Expenses Sum of the expenses Profit Gross − cost of goods − expenses Profit is negative when the event lost money. Closing and deleting Closing an event returns every unsold unit to the catalogue and makes the event read-only. An event can only be deleted while it has no sales. Its stock goes back to the catalogue. An event with sales must be closed instead, so the sales are kept. Where sales are stored Sales go to a table shared by every channel, with the channel set to EVENT and a link to the event. The future sales module will read the same table.

get-started.title: Get started
get-started.text: Get started Requirements JDK 17 or newer. For Android, the Android SDK and a device or emulator. For iOS, a Mac with Xcode. Run the app ./gradlew :desktopApp:run # run the desktop app ./gradlew :androidApp:installDebug # install on a connected Android device or emulator Try it with toy data ./gradlew :desktopApp:runDemo # run the desktop app on a database full of made-up data The demo uses its own file, musa-demo.db , next to the real one. It is deleted and filled again every time the demo starts, so you can break things freely. It holds ten products (some low on stock, one sold out), an event that closed last month, one happening today and one coming up. Your real musa.db is never touched. For iOS, open iosApp/ in Xcode on a Mac and run it from there. Run the tests ./gradlew :shared:jvmTest # run the shared tests on the JVM Where the data lives The database is a single file called musa.db ( musa-demo.db for the demo). On desktop it is stored in the per-user data folder of each system: System Folder Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/MUSA or ~/.local/share/MUSA macOS ~/Library/Application Support/MUSA Windows %APPDATA%\MUSA On Android and iOS it lives in the app's private storage. ⚠️ The schema still changes without migrations. Delete musa.db if the app fails to open after an update.

inventory.title: Inventory
inventory.text: Inventory The inventory module keeps the catalogue: what the artist sells, in which versions, at what price and how much is left. Products and variants A product is either physical or digital , and always has at least one variant. A physical product has a material, and its variants carry SKU, stock, minimum stock, weight and width, height and depth. A digital product has a delivery format and an optional turnaround in days. Its variants are levels or formats, such as "sketch" or "full colour". Each variant has its own price and cost. Money is stored as whole cents to avoid rounding errors. The margin is price minus cost, also shown as a percentage of the price. Rules on save A draft is checked before it is saved. It is rejected when: The product name is blank, or it has no variants. There are two or more variants and one has no name, or two share a name (case and accents ignored). A price, cost, stock, minimum stock or turnaround is negative. A weight or size is zero or negative. A SKU repeats, inside the product or in another product. Low stock A physical variant is low on stock when it is sold out, or when its stock is at or below its minimum. A product is low on stock when any of its variants is. Searching and filtering The product list shows active and draft products, or only archived ones. It can be narrowed by: Text, matched against name, description and SKUs, ignoring case and accents. Kind (physical or digital). Tags. A product must have every selected tag. Low stock only. Results are sorted by name. Duplicating Duplicating a product creates a new draft with new ids. On physical products the stock is reset to zero and SKUs are cleared, because a SKU must be unique.

overview.title: Overview
overview.text: Overview MUSA is a local-first inventory and business app for digital artists who also sell physical stock. It runs on Android, desktop and iOS from one Kotlin Multiplatform codebase. What it does today The first module is inventory . It keeps the artist's catalogue in a local SQLite database: Products of two kinds: physical stock (prints, stickers, merch) and digital work made to order (commissions). Variants for each product, each with its own price and cost. Physical variants also carry SKU, stock, minimum stock, weight and size. Tags with a colour from a fixed palette, used to group and filter the catalogue. Statuses : draft, active and archived. The second module is events : fairs and markets where stock is taken from the catalogue, sold on the spot, and summed up into gross, cost, expenses and profit. What it does not do It has no server and no account. One device belongs to one artist. It does not sync between devices yet. See the roadmap . Read next Get started to build and run it. Architecture to see how the code is laid out. Inventory for the rules the inventory module follows. Events for how stock, sales and profit work at a fair.

roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.text: Roadmap MUSA is built one module at a time. Inventory and events are done; the rest follow in roughly this order. Version 1, fully local [x] Inventory : products, variants, stock, prices and tags. [ ] Backups : automatic periodic copies of the local database. [ ] Accounts : income and expenses. [ ] Marketplace : listings and orders from the places the artist sells. [ ] Shipping : parcels and their state. [x] Events : fairs and markets, with the stock taken, sales, expenses and profit. [ ] Income tax : records needed for the yearly tax return. Later Optional sync with a Kotlin and Spring Boot backend, built as a modular monolith. Conflicts are resolved by last write wins, using timestamps and the UUIDs the app already generates.
